Maria (runtime): Heads-up — saw a noisy tail-latency spike in prod-dedicated today around 09:12 UTC. Workload: gpt-small, seq=8k, batch=1, fused-attn + kernel-coalesce enabled. Latency p99 ~3x baseline. Timeline shows repeated small KV write stalls during decode. Perfetto: https://perfetto.google.com/trace/?q=2612345678 nsys: s3://perf-archive/nsys-2612345678.nsight

Vikram: Ugh. Any change around kernel selector or prefetch heuristics rolled recently?

Maria (runtime): We rolled #5648 yesterday — enabled aggressive coalescing for fused attn on SM>=80. Repro steps below.

Maria (runtime): ```
# repro (dedicated replica)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python runner.py --model gpt-small --seq 8192 --batch 1 --use-fused-attn --coalesce true --kv-mode writeback
nsys profile --sample=cpu --output nsight-2612345678 ./runner.py ...
```

Jace: Can you paste the nsys kernel timeline snippet? looking for long gaps in memcpy or sysmem ops. Small writes interleaving with attn kernels usually mean serialization in KV write path.

Maria (runtime): Pasted minimal timeline (trimmed):
```
[nsys timeline]
0.000s fused_attn_forward (l1)  3.2ms
0.003s kv_write_coalesce 0.6ms
0.004s fused_attn_backward 2.9ms
0.007s kv_write_flusher 1.4ms <-- repeated every ~6ms (hotspot)
```

Olivia: I can repro on dedicated-staging. I ran with profiling flags and saw same kv_write_flusher kernel occupying many small slots. Looks like flush triggered too often (invalid coalesce threshold).

Olivia: Repro command I used: ```./runner.py --model gpt-small --seq 8192 --batch 1 --fused-attn --coalesce-threshold 32 --kv-batch 8```

Vikram: Sounds like coalesce threshold default got lowered accidentally. Which commit touched selector heuristics? @Ryan?

Ryan: That was my change (commit 3a9f7b) — I adjusted coalesce threshold to favor lower latency on short sequences. Oops — didn't gate by seq length. I'll revert the threshold tweak for long sequences.

Jace: Before revert, can we try a runtime workaround: make kernel-selector pick non-coalesced path for seq>=4096. Quick patch in selector: if seq_len >= 4096 and batch == 1 then prefer kernel_variant_no_coalesce. Small diff: ```if seq_len >= 4096 and batch_sz == 1: variant = 'no_coalesce'```

Maria (runtime): Applied that locally and re-ran — latency p99 back to baseline, kv_write_flusher occurrences dropped by ~90%. Good quick mitigation.

perf-bot: nsys summary for nsight-2612345678.nsight -> GPU active: 72%, memcpy: 6%, kernel stalls attributable to small kv_write_flusher invocations (estimate 18% extra tail). Link: s3://perf-archive/summary-2612345678.json :thumbsup:

ci-bot: regression-tests/dedicated/latency: failed on commit 3a9f7b (coalesce threshold). Test: long-seq-latency p99 degraded by 2.8x. See CI: https://ci.redwood/2612345678

Vikram: Plan: rollback commit 3a9f7b for now, then design a two-tier heuristic: aggressive coalesce only when (seq_len < 2048 OR batch_sz > 1) AND sm_version>=80 AND kv_buffer_bytes > 64k. Also add perf test for seq=8k batch=1 gating.

Ryan: I'll open PR for rollback + unit/e2e perf test. Also will add perfetto markers around KV flush path to get better flamegraph context.

Maria (runtime): Great. Can we schedule a short deep-dive today 10:30am PT? Want to bring kernel timelines, nvprof snapshots, and rollout plan.

Jace: +1. I'll bring annotated nvprof slices and a quick patch to adjust the coalesce state machine (reduce flush frequency).

Olivia: I'll attach the perfetto trace and nsys raw capture to the meeting thread.

Maria (runtime): Thanks all — saving tickets: RUNTIME-1429 (investigate kv flush frequency), RUNTIME-1430 (rollback coalesce tweak), RUNTIME-1431 (perf test for long-seq).

Ryan: I'll link PRs in RUNTIME-1430.

perf-bot: scheduled prof-run: nightly long-seq smoke at 03:00 UTC to validate rollback.

Maria (runtime): Closing loop here, but keep thread alive with any new regressions. :ear_of_rice:
